SMTO-HTTP-0007 — SMTO tried to use an HTTP connection the wrong way

GUID: 7443f824-b87c-4624-8aa4-ad003b6d110b
Slug: http-connect-required
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO's assistant asked to contact a service without setting up the connection the right way first, for example by mixing connection settings into a request. SMTO stopped it before anything was sent and normally corrects it on its own.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the Task keep going for a moment; SMTO normally corrects the request by itself. SMTO tells its assistant exactly what was wrong, and nothing was sent, so a corrected attempt is safe.
  2. If the Task stops, tell SMTO in the conversation which saved HTTP Connection to use (type @ and its name from Parameter Store), and ask it to connect with that first. Naming one saved connection removes the mix-up that caused the rejection.
  3. If you set the connection up yourself, open it in Parameter Store and select Test connection. A working saved connection gives SMTO a correct starting point to reuse.

What success looks like

  • SMTO connects and your request completes without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Before asking SMTO to repeat an earlier request that changes something on the service, check whether it already went through.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An HTTP tool call violated the connection rules: connection-only fields on http.request, more than one of connection_ref, profile_key or auth, invalid connection authentication, a non-read connection probe, or a request that must first be set up through http.connect.

What this means

  • A request misuses connection-only fields, combines selectors, lacks a required verified connection, contains invalid connection authentication, or uses a write as a connection probe. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A request misuses connection-only fields, combines selectors, lacks a required verified connection, contains invalid connection authentication, or uses a write as a connection probe.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect whether rejection came from request fields, authentication schema, selector conflict or the current verified route.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the rejected call in the run's activity: move base_url, tls, allowed_origins and test_path into http.connect, choose exactly one of connection_ref, profile_key or auth, keep connection probes read-only (GET, HEAD or OPTIONS), and reuse the returned connection_ref. Nothing was dispatched for the rejected call.
  • Correct the specific connection contract violation, establish the intended connection with http.connect and use its returned reference.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid read-only connect establishes the intended reference and subsequent requests use one accepted route.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
